comment: docs/measurement.md's pilot over the whole matrix: what each measuring job costs and adds, from the first runs that measured everything. Minutes are each job's wall time on its runner.

measure-size.measures: size of 1,350 Linux, RV64, Cortex-M, RV32 and Xtensa configurations, then RV64 instruction counts of 252

darwin-host-release-2.added_step: size of 126 configurations, within an existing job

cortex-m-programs.added_step: instruction counts of 216 configurations on four machines, about 2.5 minutes, within an existing job

push.concurrency: three Ubuntu jobs added to a push run of 73, none on macOS; the 20-job account limit already queues a push run, and the size jobs start once the release compiler is built

board-bundles.added: the timing images, built with the bundles

board legs.added: each port's time step at three runs, one leg at a time on the rig's one runner

schedule_and_dispatch.concurrency: three hosted jobs beside a boards run of eight, one of them macOS against the limit of five; the rig's legs stay one at a time

noise.instructions: compiler/tests/measure/noise/instructions.json: no spread on RV64 with QEMU's reserved address space, nor on the Cortex-M machines
